messages:
maria: Heads-up — Starlit reporting repeated 429s + token/s SLO violations on their Dedicated pool during a marketing blast. They say burst credits dropped to 0 and admission control started rejecting traffic. Customer on call now :rotating_light:

starlit-cs: seeing 429s for ~15m, latency jumps to 1.2s p95 for small completions. Request IDs: r-8a3f,r-8a4b. We were on model: redwood-open-7b-quant, dedicated-pool: pool-starlit-03.

sam-oncall: grabbing recent admission logs and autoscale events. Can you share a sample request (headers + size) that reproduces? Also pinging @arjun-infra.

maria: sample curl from the customer:```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer ****" -H "x-customer-pool: pool-starlit-03" -d '{"model":"redwood-open-7b-quant","prompt":"Summarize...","max_tokens":256,"stream":false}'``` They said high fanout (200 concurrent streams) starting at 2027-11-20T14:12Z.

arjun-infra: seeing admission-control logs for pool-starlit-03: admission window 1m token budget exhausted. Batching looked normal, but one host shows KV cache thrash and GPU util skewed: host-gpu-12 at 98% while others 60%. Noisy neighbor suspected. Also autoscaler attempted to add 2 nodes at 14:13 but host quota prevented allocation: "allocation failed: quota_exceeded: gpu.quota". devops-bot: autoscale event log -> ```[14:13:02] scale.up request x2 -> failed quota_exceeded; [14:14:00] admission: deny 429 token_budget=0```.

starlit-cs: we didn't change request shape. This started when we increased concurrency for a campaign. Anything we can do immediately?

sam-oncall: immediate mitigations: 1) ask customer to throttle to 100 concurrent for 10m to let credits refill; 2) move to fallback smaller model (redwood-open-3b) if quality acceptable; 3) we can temporarily increase pool burst credits if ops approves. Which option works for you?

tess-billing: note — manual burst credit top-ups are allowed but billable. Need written approval from Starlit PO. Also confirm they are on Reserved Dedicated plan or On-Demand (affects refill rules).

arjun-infra: reproduction steps for infra: 1) run async client with 200 concurrent short requests using same model + pool header; 2) monitor /internal/admission for token_budget and token_rate; 3) tail /var/log/redwood/kvcache on hosts to see cache-evict spikes. Quick command to repro locally in our staging:```python
# quick concurrency repro
import requests,concurrent.futures
URL='https://staging.redwood.local/v1/generate'
def call():
  return requests.post(URL, json={"model":"redwood-open-7b-quant","prompt":"x","max_tokens":64}, headers={"Authorization":"Bearer STAGE","x-customer-pool":"pool-starlit-03"}, timeout=10)
with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=200) as e:
  results=[e.submit(call) for _ in range(200)]
``` Capture admission log lines like: `admission: borrow_tokens=0 token_budget=0 queue=12` and GPU per-host metric: `gpu_util{host="host-gpu-12"} 0.98`.

sam-oncall: action items: - arjun: dig host-gpu-12 process (nvtop, dmesg) and check if colocated batches from another tenant cause KV cache eviction. - tess: confirm Starlit billing tier and whether ops can approve an emergency +200k token credit top-up. - maria: coordinate with customer to throttle to 100 concurrent and optionally switch to 3b fallback. I'll watch admission metrics and flip a fail-open if safe.

arjun-infra: quick check: host-gpu-12 shows high memcpy stalls and saw repeated kernel OOM logs around 14:12:45 — likely memory pressure from a heavy prompt size from another tenant. I'll isolate processes and repro with local cgroups. If noisy neighbor confirmed, next step is to throttle that tenant or migrate their jobs.

starlit-cs: we approve a small paid top-up to buy time — please send invoice and confirm amount. Also we'll throttle to 100 concurrent now and report back in 5m.

tess-billing: noted, sending invoice template to Starlit PO. For ops: suggest provisional +250k burst credits, one-time, billable.

devops-bot: system note: admission-controller: pool-starlit-03 burst_credits=0 -> after manual_credit_topup(+250000) burst_credits=250000 at 14:18:33 by tess-billing. Autoscale remains blocked by quota.

sam-oncall: OK credits top-up applied. Monitoring admission: token budget climbing; p95 latency improving from 1.2s -> 0.45s within 90s. But autoscaler still blocked. We need long-term: increase pool reserved capacity or fix quota.

arjun-infra: follow-ups: - open ticket with infra-quotas to increase gpu.quota for the cluster; - add fairshare enforcement improvements so single-host noisy workloads are isolated (KV cache pinning + per-host slice); - postmortem to update playbook to include immediate host isolation step. I'll capture kernel logs and container PIDs and attach to the support ticket.

maria: scheduling a 30m post-incident review tomorrow 09:30 UTC with Starlit and owners (arjun, sam, tess). Playbook actions: add a step to escalate for quota_exceeded on scale.up, and a checklist for emergency credit top-up.

starlit-cs: thank you — traffic reduced, latency looks much better. We'll continue to monitor and share metrics. Appreciate the quick help. :heart:

sam-oncall: closing loop for now. Repro ticket created: INCIDENT-2027-5732, owner arjun-infra. Will keep thread updated.
